To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of dissolution is faster for ions in crystals of alkali halides having different sizes than in crystals having the same sizes.

the rate of dissolution is lower in crystals with cations and anion of a similar size, and that the coordination number of the cation and anion in ion pairs and ion clusters is lower in crystals of salts with a higher solubility.
molecular dynamics simulation and solution X-ray diffraetion measurements have revealed the dissolution and nucleati on phenomena at a molecular le vel for a variety of salts in water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanism of dissolution and nucleation processes of salt crystals in water at the molecular level.
a study of the dissolution phenomena of salts in aqueous solutions, using molecular dynamics (MD) and supporting solution XRD experiments.
the development of new methods and approaches to elucidate dissolution and nucleation processes of salts in water at a molecular level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dissolution of salts in water at room temperature proceeds in two distinct steps: the initial step is the dissociation of ions from the crystal lattice and the second one is the formation of ion pairs or clusters.
the dissolution and nucleations of salts in water at room temperature are determined by the size of ions in the salts.
the dissolution rate of ions is lower when the size of cations and anion are similar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of dissolution and formation of ionic clusters is lower for crystals having cations and anion of similar size.
the dissolution of ions in water proceeds in a stepwise manner, i.e. the anions dissolve first and then the cations.
the rate of dissolution is higher in crystals having the ions of different sizes than in those with similar sizes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MD simulations can be used to study the dissolution and nucleations phenomena of salts in a water at a molecular level.
MD simulations can provide detailed molecular-level insights into the dissolution and nucleaton phenomena for salts in water, which cannot be obtained by other methods.

MD simulations are useful to elucidate the molecular level phenomena of the dissolution and nucleations of salts in water, and the results obtained by MD simulations are consistent with those by solution X-ray diffractions.
